slot.brief: Given initial amount and fraction remaining after time t, find the half-life (or time for N half-lives) using count-half-lives logic.

stem: A first-order reaction leaves $\dfrac{1}{8}$ of its initial amount after $6$ h. What is its half-life?

verdicts.working: Since $1/8=(1/2)^3$, 6 h corresponds to 3 half-lives; therefore $t_{1/2}=6/3=2$ h.

working:
$\dfrac{N}{N_0}=\left(\dfrac12\right)^n=\dfrac18=\left(\dfrac12\right)^3$\n$n=3$; $t_{1/2}=\dfrac{6\ \text{h}}{3}=2\ \text{h}$.

Independent check: Since $1/8=(1/2)^3$, 6 h corresponds to 3 half-lives; therefore $t_{1/2}=6/3=2$ h.
solution:
For a first-order reaction, $N/N_0=(1/2)^n$. Since $1/8=(1/2)^3$, 6 h corresponds to 3 half-lives.
$$t_{1/2}=\frac{6\text{ h}}{3}=2\text{ h}$$
